children.text: Degenerative and Reduction Processes in Chum Juveniles Olfactory Epithelium (Oncorhynchus keta Walbaum: Salmoniformes) at Acute Effect of Copper and Zinc Salts

Electronic microscope research of chum juveniles olfactory epithelium is conducted before and after effect of copper and zinc salts. Some singularities destruction and recovery of olfactory epithelium cells are circumscribed. Information about terms of regeneration of the cells separate types are adduced.
Research of influence of copper salts (concentration 30 mkg/l, 60 mkg/l, 190 mkg/l) and zinc (concentration 100 mkg/l) on olfactory epithelium juvenile of chum salmon.

Publication Title: Normal pressure altitude charts for the Northern Hemisphere.

Effect of Mesoscale Anticyclonic Eddies on the Hydrochemical Structure of the Bering Sea

The paper presents data showing the effect of mesoscale eddies on the
     distribution of phosphates, nitrates, ammonia nitrogen, organic phosphorus
     and nitrogen in the Bering Sea. An important role is played by powerful
     anticyclonic eddies along the edge of the continental slope. Water 'slips' over
     the slope sometimes down to depths of 600-1000 m and reaches the oxygen
     minimum layer. Under these conditions renewal of water in the oxygen
     minimum layer and upwelling of deep water in the adjacent cyclonic eddies
     take place. The new data call for revision of earlier ideas on the rate of vertical
     surface, intermediate and deep water exchange.
To show the effect of mesoscale anticyclonic eddies on the hydrochemical structure of the Bering Sea.

Distribution Patterns of Urea in the Bering Sea and its Role in the Nitrogen Cycle

Urea determination data along 5 sections in the Bering Sea perpendicular to
        the coastline show that the distribution of urea is similar to that of ammonium
        nitrogen. Accumulation of urea and ammonium was generally observed under
        the thermocline but the absolute concentration of urea was slightly higher. With
        the total urea and ammonium content of 7-10 mu g-at N/l in the euphotic
        layer, 8-10g C/m super(2) organic matter per day may be produced in the
        process of photosynthesis due to nitrogen recycling.
To report on the distribution patterns of urea in the Bering Sea and its role in the nitrogen cycle.
